# RFC-0012: Repository-authoritative multi-agent coordination

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @govctl-org

**References:** [RFC-0000](../rfc/RFC-0000.md), [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md), [RFC-0010](../rfc/RFC-0010.md), [RFC-0011](../rfc/RFC-0011.md)

## 1. Summary

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0012:C-AUTHORITY] Canonical repository authority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-authority"></a>

In repository publication mode, the configured canonical repository's main branch MUST be the authority for shared request and execution-ownership state. An update MUST become effective only after successful publication on that branch and protocol validation against its actual predecessor. Unpublished local records and unmerged pull requests MUST NOT grant execution ownership. Invalid or unauthorized records MUST NOT confer execution rights. Independent clones observing the same accepted history and policy context MUST derive the same shared state.

### [RFC-0012:C-REQUEST] Attached requests and operation identity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-request"></a>

A collaboration request MUST attach to an existing RFC, ADR or Work Item and identify its stable request identity, requested operation and exact input revision. That operation and input binding MUST be immutable; a different operation or input MUST require a new request identity. Claims MUST reference their request and its input binding. Completed or cancelled requests MUST NOT be claimed again or accept another completion. Requests, claims, handoffs and results MUST remain attached records rather than new governed task artifacts. Each state-changing operation MUST have a stable identity and semantic payload, including its actor, target and references to the state it changes. The same operation identity with different semantic content MUST be rejected; a retry with the same content MUST return the existing accepted result without duplicating its effects, including after request completion. A publication-parent witness MAY change during a retry without changing the operation's semantic intent.

### [RFC-0012:C-EXCLUSION] Exclusive modification and parallel review (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-exclusion"></a>

At most one current execution claim MUST authorize execution of a given request, including a read-only review request. A modifying request MUST additionally hold exclusive write claims for every existing artifact it changes; at most one current write claim MUST authorize modification of a given artifact. A modifying result MUST identify its full write scope, and its publication MUST be rejected unless its executing holder has the required current claims for that scope. New artifact identities MUST remain unique in accepted repository state. Distinct read-only review requests for the same immutable revision MAY run concurrently and MUST NOT acquire artifact write ownership merely by reviewing. A request that changes an artifact's lifecycle MUST satisfy the same write-ownership rules as a content modification, in addition to the existing lifecycle and verification requirements.

### [RFC-0012:C-PUBLICATION] Conditional publication and semantic revalidation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-publication"></a>

An accepted coordination update MUST advance canonical main by a conditional fast-forward against the exact authoritative parent used for its validation. Forced updates MUST NOT be accepted as protocol publication. A stale publication parent or conflicting claim MUST cause a conflict rather than silently granting authority. Granting execution authority or accepting an effective result against a changed input revision MUST cause a conflict. Changed input alone MUST NOT prevent cancellation, claim release or publication of explicitly ineffective history; those operations MUST still satisfy their applicable authorization and causal-state requirements. After a publication race, retrying clients MUST validate the operation against the newly observed authoritative state; a successful textual rebase alone MUST NOT establish semantic validity. When branch protection requires pull requests or a merge queue, the same conditions MUST hold at the final main update, and ownership MUST remain ineffective until that update succeeds.

### [RFC-0012:C-GENERATION] Claim generations and explicit transfer (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-generation"></a>

Accepted ownership transitions MUST use monotonically increasing generations for each request and each artifact write scope so that a previous holder cannot regain authority by replaying an old operation. A handoff or takeover MUST name the affected scopes, their prior generations and the new holder, and MUST atomically invalidate the prior holder's authority over those scopes. The resulting claims MUST satisfy [RFC-0012:C-EXCLUSION](../rfc/RFC-0012.md#rfc-0012c-exclusion). Takeover MUST include an explicit authorization decision and reason. Release, cancellation and completion MUST invalidate the affected claims for future results; an idempotent replay of an already accepted result remains valid under [RFC-0012:C-REQUEST](../rfc/RFC-0012.md#rfc-0012c-request). This version MUST NOT infer takeover or release solely from wall-clock age, a missing heartbeat or an unavailable process. Results from obsolete generations MUST NOT mutate artifacts or complete the current request.

### [RFC-0012:C-RESULT] Revision-bound results and code targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-result"></a>

Under the publication capability, a result MUST identify its request, actor, exact input revision, applicable request-claim generation and immutable outcome or resulting revision. An effective result MUST reference the current request-claim generation and, for a modifying result, all applicable current artifact write-claim generations at publication. A review MUST remain bound to the reviewed document digest and, for code review, an explicit immutable code commit; that code commit MUST NOT be inferred from the current coordination main HEAD. Coordination-only commits MUST NOT invalidate an approval whose document and code targets remain unchanged. Obsolete results MAY remain as explicitly ineffective history but MUST NOT be rebound to a newer input, claim or code revision. Accepted results MUST NOT bypass existing artifact lifecycle or guard requirements. These publication-mode bindings MUST NOT retroactively change the targets or interpretation of existing standalone collaboration records.

### [RFC-0012:C-POLICY] External authorization and explicit policy context (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-policy"></a>

Runtime scheduling, participant authentication, signer-to-subject bindings, permission management and credentials MUST remain responsibilities of external clients or authorities. govctl MUST validate protocol structure, revision bindings and causal state using explicit authorization and policy context supplied for the operation. An authorization decision MUST identify the authority and policy revision used without persisting credentials. A repository-embedded key, an asserted role or Git push permission alone MUST NOT establish an actor's execution or approval authority. Approval requirements and transfer permissions MUST be supplied explicitly by the governing policy rather than inferred from a particular orchestration product.

### [RFC-0012:C-COMPATIBILITY] Capability and existing-history compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-compatibility"></a>

Publication-mode clients MUST negotiate an explicit capability before relying on cross-clone execution ownership or publication-mode review targets. An unsupported capability MUST produce an unsupported-operation result rather than falling back to clone-local claims. Existing formatVersion 1 and 2 collaboration records MUST retain their bytes, identities and interpretation under [RFC-0011:C-COMPATIBILITY](../rfc/RFC-0011.md#rfc-0011c-compatibility); migration MUST NOT turn historical assignments or execution receipts into current ownership, or rebind historical reviews to publication-mode targets. The local claims, reservations and presence defined by [RFC-0010](../rfc/RFC-0010.md) MUST remain clone-local and MUST NOT be treated as distributed ownership witnesses. Existing standalone artifact commands and read-only views MUST remain usable without enabling repository publication mode.
